segments.expected: Kiva had never seen a thing die all at once like that. The kiddle at Gannet Creek had been cut three posts at a time, and then four, and had gone to ash in the mud slowly, over the low water, while she was walking away from it in the dark. This went at once. The two stumps went grey and soft and slumped in the mud like candles in a hot room. The mouth went grey. The sleeve, lying in its fold on the bank and across the mud, went grey all along its length, and then thin, and then it was a film of ash lying on the mud like dust on a sill.

She did not know it then. She knew only that her two fingers were on the ash pole and they said nothing, still, nothing, the slack holding, the water still, the grass still, the thread lying in its bed like a ribbon. segments.expected: It leaned inland, a hair, the way the upper stow's post had leaned at ten to eleven before the gust had reached it. Only there was no gust. There was no flood. The water had not moved. Kiva's fingers on the pole said that the water had not moved, and the grass on the west bank stood up straight, and the thread lay in its bed. And the far post of the Tarn's stow leaned inland on the turn of a tide that had not turned.
